messages.content:
Sarunyu has a stick of length 1 with one endpoint marked in red. Every minute, he picks one of his sticks uniformly at random and breaks it into two halves of equal length. Compute the expected length of the stick with the red endpoint after 5 minutes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(L_n\) be the length of the stick with the red endpoint after \(n\) minutes.

Before the \(n\)-th break, there are \(n\) sticks total, exactly one of which has the red endpoint. So the red stick is chosen with probability \(1/n\).

- If it is chosen, its length is halved.
- If it is not chosen, its length stays the same.

Thus,
\[
\mathbb{E}[L_n \mid \text{past}]
= \frac1n\cdot \frac{L_{n-1}}2 + \left(1-\frac1n\right)L_{n-1}
= \left(1-\frac1{2n}\right)L_{n-1}.
\]

Taking expectations and starting from \(L_0=1\),
\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
= \prod_{n=1}^5 \left(1-\frac1{2n}\right)
= \frac12\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac56\cdot\frac78\cdot\frac9{10}
= \frac{63}{256}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{63}{256}}
\]
